summary: הָיָה says that someone or something exists, is in a condition, becomes something, or happens. With a person and לְ it can express possession or a relationship; with עִם it can express presence and help. Its Aramaic counterpart הֲוָא carries these uses in Daniel and Ezra and in the Peshitta.

senses.definition: Be present or exist, or be in a stated condition or place.

evidence.note: The earth was formless and empty: a condition, not a change expressed by the verb itself.
No shrub was yet in the earth.

senses.definition: Come to be what the following expression names.

evidence.note: The man became a living נֶפֶשׁ.
The woman became a pillar of salt.

senses.definition: Introduce an occurrence or mark its taking place in time.

evidence.note: After these things, the testing of Abraham takes place.
God speaks, and light comes to be.

senses.gloss: belong to; stand in a relationship
senses.definition: With לְ, be someone’s possession, people, God, or other stated relation.

evidence.note: Livestock and servants belonged to Abram.
I will be their God, and they will be my people.

senses.definition: Be present with someone; where the context promises help, support that person.

evidence.note: אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ promises Moses God’s presence.
יַהְוֶה was with Joseph, and Joseph prospered.

stems.gloss: happen; become; be brought into a condition

senses.definition: Of an event that comes about, often something exceptional.

evidence.note: A cry unlike anything that has happened before.
Today you have become a people to יַהְוֶה.

senses.definition: In Daniel’s account, be left overcome or spent. The precise force in these two passages is less certain than the ordinary sense “happen”.

evidence.note: Daniel was overcome and ill for days.
The king’s spirit is troubled and his sleep is gone.

phrases.gloss: I will be who I will be

evidence.note: The same אֶהְיֶה as in the promise of 3:12; the formula is God’s answer to Moses’s question about his name.

senses.definition: Exist in a condition, or come into it.

evidence.note: May God’s name be blessed.
Your dwelling will be with the animals.

senses.definition: Come about, including a future event.

evidence.note: What will happen at the end of days.

senses.definition: Come into existence or a stated condition.

evidence.note: The Peshitta says that everything came to be through him.
The word became flesh.
All this happened so that what was spoken would be fulfilled.

cognates.note: The Akkadian verb supplies a comparison for becoming, rather than every use of Hebrew “be”.

doctrine.statement: In Exodus 3:12 יַהְוֶה answers Moses’s fear with אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ, “I will be with you”; in 3:14 he uses אֶהְיֶה in answering the question about his name. The name-answer belongs to this promise of his own presence and action. The verb itself also describes ordinary created things and does not by itself define a divine attribute.

note: Mic 2:4 נִהְיָה is filed by spelling but analysed under נהה, and is not evidence for this verb. The Aramaic הֲוָא words are included under their own root key; the brief for היה does not find them automatically. The special Niphal uses in Dan 2:1 and 8:27 need review. No separate derivation of the divine name is asserted. The database root key is הוא for both Aramaic forms; it is a verb here, distinct from the pronoun of the same consonants.
